headline: DELTA RESOURCES EXTENDS I-ZONE GOLD 400+ METRES IN THUNDER BAY — 4.85 g/t AU OVER 8.0M IN INITIAL CHANNEL SAMPLING
snippet: Delta Resources Ltd. (TSXV: DLTA) reported initial channel-sampling results extending the I-Zone gold discovery at the Delta-1 Gold Project, approximately 50 km west of Thunder Bay, by more than 400 metres eastward. Highlight intercepts include 4.85 g/t Au over 8.0 metres (trench D1-26-TR17) and 4.23 g/t Au over 4.3 metres (D1-26-TR20), with individual outcrop samples up to 16.1 g/t Au confirming high-grade vein continuity into the new area. The I-Zone remains open along strike in both directions and largely untested at depth — a combination that sets up material resource estimate upside if the follow-up diamond drill program confirms the channel results.

headline: COPPER RECOVERS TO $14,660/TONNE MONDAY ON CHINA DEMAND SURGE — GRASBERG FORCE MAJEURE AND QBM CHILE CUT UNDERPIN BULL CASE
snippet: LME copper climbed 1.44% on Monday to approximately US$14,660 per tonne, recovering from last week's pullback from the September 10 all-time high of US$14,875, driven by rising Chinese physical demand — the Yangshan copper import premium climbed to $121 per tonne, its highest level since November 2022. Structural supply remains constrained: Freeport-McMoRan's Grasberg mine declared force majeure following a September mudslide, removing an estimated 591,000 tonnes from 2025–2026 output, while Quebrada Blanca in Chile downgraded production guidance due to operational challenges. Copper is now up 16% in 2026 and tracking Thursday's Trump-Xi summit as a near-term binary for tariff flows and trade rhetoric that could add or remove a further $300–500/tonne in either direction.

headline: CANADIAN COPPER HITS BROAD SULPHIDE ZONES IN ALL 5 HOLES WEST OF MURRAY BROOK — EXPANDING NB VMS DEPOSIT AHEAD OF PRODUCTION DECISION
snippet: Canadian Copper Inc. (CSE: CCI) reported that five consecutive 2026 diamond drill holes (MB26-06 to MB26-10) all intersected broad sulphide-bearing zones along the western margin of the Murray Brook VMS deposit in New Brunswick, extending the known sulphide system 25 metres west of the current deposit footprint. Chalcopyrite was observed in all five holes and sphalerite in selected intervals; assay results are pending. The prior comparable western hole (MB19-01) returned 26.4 metres at 1.35% Cu from 26.0 metres — setting a benchmark for expected grades against an existing resource of 21.1 million tonnes at 0.45% Cu, 0.91% Pb, and 2.49% Zn. Canadian Copper secured up to C$70M in project financing earlier in 2026, making this drill extension a direct read on mineable resource tonnage.

headline: SERABI GOLD HITS 37.10 g/t AU AT CORINGA AND 11.85 g/t AU AT PALITO — 32,000M BROWNFIELD CAMPAIGN TARGETING 1.5MOZ INVENTORY BY Q1 2027
snippet: Serabi Gold Plc (AIM: SRB) published its Phase II brownfield exploration update from 20,831 metres drilled across 79 holes at the Palito Complex and Coringa Mine in Pará State, Brazil. Highlight intercepts include 0.42 metres at 37.10 g/t Au at Serra South (Coringa) and 1.38 metres at 11.85 g/t Au at the same zone, plus 0.82 metres at 3.99 g/t Au at Senna (Palito Complex). Six rigs are active across both sites; the full 32,000-metre programme runs through October 2026 with an updated mineral resource estimate targeting 1.5Moz combined inventory expected in Q1 2027. At gold above US$4,370/oz, the economics of the company's existing gold production make this incremental resource addition materially cash-flow relevant.

headline: SILVER LOGS 6TH CONSECUTIVE ANNUAL DEFICIT AT 46.3MOZ — 762MOZ CUMULATIVE INVENTORY DRAW SINCE 2021 AS INDUSTRIAL DEMAND SHOWS NO SIGNS OF EASING
snippet: The Silver Institute's World Silver Survey 2026 confirms a projected sixth consecutive annual supply deficit of 46.3 million troy ounces — 15% wider than the 40.3 million ounce shortfall recorded in 2025. Cumulative drawdowns since 2021 now total 762 million ounces. Most silver is extracted as a byproduct of gold, copper, and zinc mining, making higher silver prices structurally unable to incentivise dedicated new mine supply on any short timeline. Industrial demand — EVs, solar panels, electronics, and AI data-centre components — remains effectively inelastic, while recycling volumes, though rising to multi-year highs, have not closed the gap. At current spot of approximately $67/oz, the gold-to-silver ratio sits near 65:1, compared to a 2011 low of 32:1, a spread many analysts consider historically anomalous given converging fundamentals.

headline: URANIUM LONG-TERM CONTRACT PRICE HITS $96.50/LB — NOMINAL ALL-TIME HIGH ABOVE 2007 RECORD AS UTILITIES PAY $7/LB PREMIUM OVER SPOT
snippet: Uranium long-term contract prices closed August 2026 at $96.50 per pound U3O8 — a nominal all-time high, surpassing the $95/lb peak set in 2007 — according to UxC and TradeTech month-end averages published by Cameco. With spot around $90/lb, the $6-7/lb term premium signals that large nuclear fuel buyers are paying a forward scarcity premium to lock in multi-year supply years ahead of projected delivery dates. Crux Investor's analysis frames this as the clearest confirmation yet that institutional uranium buyers have concluded future supply is structurally tighter than current spot volumes suggest — a thesis validated by simultaneous production guidance reductions from both Cameco and Kazatomprom.

headline: GREAT PACIFIC GOLD MAIDEN DRILL CONFIRMS LARGE MAGMATIC-HYDROTHERMAL SYSTEM AT KASIE RIDGE — ADVANCED ARGILLIC ALTERATION 315M WIDE, OPEN AT DEPTH IN PNG
snippet: Great Pacific Gold Corp. (TSXV: GPAC) reported maiden drill results from the Kasie Ridge target at its Wild Dog Project in East New Britain Province, Papua New Guinea. Two holes (KAS-01A at 595.7m and KAS-02 at 346.6m) confirmed correlated silica-rich and advanced argillic alteration across a 315-metre corridor, with KAS-02 intersecting eight gold-bearing sample intervals grading 0.20–1.55 g/t Au across two structurally controlled zones. KAS-01A terminated within the strongest sulphide-rich alteration encountered, leaving the system open at depth — the classic setup for an epithermal or porphyry gold system requiring deeper follow-up drilling. Kasie Ridge is the project's largest preserved advanced argillic alteration target, adjacent to the Magiabe and Mengmut discoveries already confirmed on the same Wild Dog land package.

headline: INFLECTION RESOURCES ADDS 2,660 km² OF UNDRILLED IOCG TARGETS ADJACENT TO OLYMPIC DAM — 7 COPPER-GOLD TARGETS IN GAWLER CRATON, SOUTH AUSTRALIA
snippet: Inflection Resources Ltd. (CSE: AUCU) announced the addition of the Fortitude Project — 2,660 km² of 100%-owned, royalty-free exploration licences in South Australia's Gawler Craton — hosting seven high-priority, undrilled targets prospective for IOCG and ISCG copper-gold systems, plus a discrete gold target. The licences sit approximately 290 km northwest of BHP's Olympic Dam mine, adjacent to Oak Dam, Carrapateena, and Prominent Hill — world-class deposits that validate the mineral system scale the Gawler Craton can host. The Fortitude acquisition complements existing AngloGold Ashanti-partnered ground in New South Wales, making Inflection a multi-jurisdiction IOCG consolidator at a time when non-Chinese critical mineral land is attracting sustained strategic capital.

headline: COT REPORT SEPT 18: GOLD SPEC LONGS TRIM AFTER FED HIKE BUT SILVER POSITIONING MOST EXTENDED IN 6 MONTHS — TRUMP-XI SUMMIT THE SWING FACTOR
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly Commitments of Traders analysis for the September 15 positioning snapshot shows large speculators trimming gold net longs in the week following the Federal Reserve's September 17 rate hike, while maintaining an elevated net long position overall. Silver's large spec net long is at its most extended reading in approximately six months — either reflecting conviction on the structural deficit and industrial demand thesis, or a crowded positioning that could amplify a reversal on any macro shock. The US dollar index commercial positioning remained net short for the fourth consecutive week, a configuration that has historically supported precious metals when geopolitical sentiment is constructive — with Thursday's Trump-Xi summit in Washington as the key directional catalyst for the week.

headline: KING COPPER DOUBLES COLQUEMAYO LAND TO 7,170 NEW HECTARES IN PERU'S EMERGING COPPER DISTRICT — CONSOLIDATING GROUND AHEAD OF DRILL PROGRAM
snippet: King Copper Discovery Corp. announced that its Peruvian operating subsidiary Aurora Copper Peru SAC has received approval for eight additional concessions adding approximately 7,170 hectares of contiguous exploration claims to the north of the Colquemayo Copper Project, doubling the company's total land position in this emerging southern Peru copper district. The expanded footprint, which now sits within the proven copper-porphyry belt adjacent to large producing operations, materially increases the opportunity for new discoveries across the district ahead of a planned drill program. Peru's copper-porphyry belt has historically hosted world-class deposits at depths accessible to exploration drilling, and continued consolidation of ground in this corridor reflects broader sector competition for drill-ready copper targets.
